facts.statement: The species Panamericansaurus schroederi was named and described by Jorge Orlando Calvo and Juan Domingo Porfiri in 2010.
facts.quote: The type species Panamericansaurus schroederi was named and described by Jorge Orlando Calvo and Juan Domingo Porfiri in 2010.

facts.statement: The genus name Panamericansaurus honors the Pan American Energy company that funded the research.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the Pan American Energy company which financially supported the paleontological investigations.

facts.statement: The species name schroederi honors the Schroeder family who owned the land where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the Schroeder family on whose land the remains were found.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MUCPv-417 was found in June 2003 in the Allen Formation near San Patricio del Chañar, Neuquén, Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype, MUCPv-417, was found in June 2003 in a layer of the Allen Formation (Campanian-Maastrichtian) near San Patricio del Chañar, in Neuquén, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype's left humerus measures 123 centimeters in length.
The estimated total length of the holotype individual is 11 meters.
facts.quote: The length of the holotype individual has been estimated at 11 m.

facts.statement: Panamericansaurus is classified within the clade Aeolosaurini of the family Titanosauridae, alongside Aeolosaurus and Gondwanatitan.
facts.quote: The describers placed Panamericansaurus in a clade within the Titanosauridae, the Aeolosaurini, of which also Aeolosaurus and Gondwanatitan are also members.

facts.statement: Panamericansaurus lived between 75 and 70 million years ago during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del geológico Cretácico entre 75 a 70 millones de años durante el Campaniense y Maastrichtiense en lo que hoy es América del Sur.

facts.statement: Panamericansaurus is very similar to Aeolosaurus, with which it is closely related, differing only in vertebral details.
facts.quote: Panamericansaurus es muy similar al Aeolosaurus, con el que está estrechamente emparentado, del que difiere sólo en detalles de las vértebras.

facts.statement: The time range for Panamericansaurus is the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
